title: Deor and interlocking rune streams

reader_test.input: The rune text of LP2-03 and the archived Old English poem Deor.
reader_test.action: Split runes by whether their zero-based alphabet number is prime, try Deor as a key for that group, then use its best output as a repeating key for the other group.
reader_test.check: Check whether the original score thresholds can be reached, and separately compare rescaled scores from the full two-stage search with 199 shuffled pages.

question: Does the archived prime-index split and Deor-to-derived-key sequence produce a distinctive second-stream IoC on current LP2-03?
reader_question: Can Deor unlock one stream and use it to unlock the rest?
summary: The original source hit thresholds are impossible for its raw score. A separately normalized whole-procedure control finds no distinctive final-stage peak in this bounded test.
finding: The original hit conditions cannot be satisfied: raw IoC is at most 1, while the program requires more than 1.3 or 1.5. On LP2-03, its selected first-stage candidate adds Deor at offset 47 and scores 0.0649; the second subtracts the selected key at offset 31 and scores 0.0404. A separate normalized comparison gives a second-stage maximum of 1.173, reached or exceeded by 110 of 199 whole-procedure shuffles. The first-stage maximum is 1.882, reached by 18 of 199 shuffles.
limitations: Zero original source HIT rows are not negative evidence because the gates cannot pass. The normalized test was frozen separately and measures only one page, one pinned Deor stream, a prime-index partition, the source direction/offset grids and one histogram-preserving shuffle model. Synthetic controls verify arithmetic, not power to detect English. Other two-stream ciphers remain untested.
next_steps: A stronger proposal should specify how the streams are separated, how the first output keys the second, and a full expected reading or held-out prediction before inspecting the result.

scope.representation: Current LP2-03 canonical GP29 rune values, exactly matching archived old page_20 after filtering; split by whether rune index is prime.
scope.procedure: Replay original code in a temp folder; independently run all 1,800 first-stage Deor variants, select maximum raw IoC, then all 195 repeating-derived-key variants, retaining original unreachable HIT gates. Separately compare 29×normalized maxima with 199 whole-procedure page shuffles.
scope.parameters: 217 runes:65 prime-index,152 other; source Old English Deor parser yields960 values; 3 modes×600 offsets and3 modes×65 repeat offsets; 29 Caesar shifts; 199 seeded page shuffles, seed20261023.
scope.exclusions: Other pages, alternative prime definitions/partitions, modern Deor translation, other poems, word resets, variable key feedback, other language scores and all untested stream rules.

review.kind: exact archived-source replay plus separately declared normalized diagnostic
review.reviewer: Unchanged source stdout matches archived input; independent selected-decode arithmetic and full 199-control rerun; parser amendment retains initial failed exploratory result.

reproduction.environment: Python3 standard library. Exact original-script replay additionally requires a local checkout of pinned upstream revision bf89d3d13aad2b8f2c95ab195cf1b092f250775c.

visuals.caption: The original raw-score thresholds cannot be reached; a separate normalized full-search comparison finds no unusual final-stage peak.
